title: Smoking Linked with Increased Loneliness
paragraphs: It is well known that smoking is harmful to people's physical health. However, a new study from Europe suggests that it may also be linked to people's social health, and in particular to loneliness.

The study was presented in September 2026 at the European Respiratory Society Congress in Barcelona, Spain, by Dr. Keir Philip of Imperial College London. The researchers used data from the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe, a large long-term study of older adults. They analyzed information on more than 50,000 people in 15 European countries, who had an average age of 67.

To measure loneliness, the researchers used a well-known set of questions that asks people how often they feel that they lack companionship, feel left out or feel isolated from others. They compared the answers of people who currently smoked with those of people who did not smoke. Two years later, the participants answered the same questions again.

The results showed that people who smoked were lonelier than people who did not smoke, even after the researchers took into account other factors such as age and gender. In addition, smokers' loneliness increased more over the two-year period than that of non-smokers. According to the researchers, this pattern was broadly the same across Europe.
As Philip explained, although it is known that smoking is bad for physical health, little is known about what it does to people's social health.

The researchers have suggested several possible explanations. For example, illnesses related to smoking may make it harder for people to move around, which could make it more difficult to take part in social activities. In addition, because smoking is now banned in many public places and homes, people who smoke may have fewer opportunities to socialize.

However, the study does not prove that smoking causes loneliness. In fact, the link could work in both directions. Previous research has suggested that loneliness may lead some people to start smoking. The study has also not yet been published in a scientific journal.
